$comment: EXP-1707 (epic #EXP-1704, Danny 2026-11-06): THE MERGE TRAIN, server-side, replaces yolo mode (session-chat.json EXP-1413) and the person's Merge pill. TS reference src/merge-train.ts; the server worker (#EXP-1709) and the pipeline (#EXP-1708) apply it; the clients (#EXP-1710, one PR per platform) replay `statusPill`, `menu`, `stuckRow` ×4 (natives replay this file by path like every fixture: registering it breaks no leg). MODE: `teams.merge_mode` (contract teamMergeMode) replaces `teams.yolo_mode`: `auto` = DEFAULT for every team, self-hosted included; `approval` = a ready PR waits for a person's Needs approval, then queues. Settings: the yolo switch becomes ONE select row `copy.settings` (Automatic | After approval), owners only. STATE: `pull_requests.merge_state` (contract prMergeState) + `merge_attempts` (train bounces) + `merge_hold` (the hold reason, null = none) + the 24 h clock (`queuedSince`, first entry to queued) + `mergeNow`. draft | checks | queued | testing | merged | conflict | failing | held. READINESS (`readiness`, `mergeWait`, first blocker wins): draft → `draft`; its OWN head checks red (prChecksState failure) → `failing`; running → `checks` (#EXP-1711: over the GATED checks, pr-checks.json `gatedChecks`: the base branch's required checks when it names any, else every check; an informational leg never holds a PR); the OPENER or any descendant of it not idle (queued, running/busy: today yolo waits for the whole chat, the train only for the opener's subtree) → `session`; `approval` mode and nobody pressed Needs approval → `approval`; else READY (checks green or none). `preTrainState`: ready = queued; draft = draft; failing = failing; any other wait = checks. Every lifecycle edge (turn end, session end, pr open/update, a checks change, a push) re-evaluates readiness; the watchdog tick too. STATE MACHINE (`steps`, `mergeStep(pr, event)` → {pr, post}; merged is final): readiness moves only draft/checks/queued/conflict/failing (testing, held never; a Merge now PR is queued unless it is a draft); `push` (a new head) = checks again with attempts 0 (Danny 2026-11-08, #EXP-1711: a new push resets the bounce count, so an agent rebasing against a busy master never runs out of bounces; a testing unit is pulled from its run: the worker recomposes the batch without it); a PR held for `bounces` is revived by a push the same way (its agent is back), while a person's hold and a `timeout` hold stay held, and the 24 h clock (queuedSince) is never reset by a push: an abandoned PR is still held after 3 bounces or 24 h; `train_start` queued → testing; `train_landed` testing → merged (post merged); `train_requeued` testing → queued (an innocent unit of a red batch, a cancelled run); `train_conflict` / `train_failing` testing → conflict / failing and attempts + 1 (a BOUNCE: the PR goes back to its agent, post conflict / failing); the bounce that reaches `limits.bounces` (3) lands in held (holdReason bounces, post held, never conflict/failing); `tick` = held (timeout, post held) once `limits.hours` (24) passed since queuedSince in checks/queued/conflict/failing (testing finishes first; a Merge now is exempt); `hold` (a person, any state but draft/held/merged) = held (person, post held; a testing unit is pulled from its run); `resume` (= Needs you Retry) held → checks with attempts 0, the clock and the hold cleared; `merge_now` (owners; MCP `pr merge {force: true}` from a team owner or a team agent's session, #EXP-1711: one busy lane never holds a finished PR) = queued at the FRONT, alone, UNTESTED: the train composes it on the base (resolvers run; any other conflict bounces as usual) and fast-forwards without CI; it clears a hold, keeps attempts. A pre-train red (own checks) is `failing` without a bounce and without pr_merge: the pr_checks wake (pr-checks.json) already told the agent. LANDING: fast-forward the base (master) to the EXACT tested train commit (expected old sha; base moved = recompose); the App sits on the base ruleset's bypass list. #FEED-212: a landing is REPORTED (the merged line, the PR closed on the forge, pr_merged and its issue moves) only once the forge CONFIRMS it (`landing`, `landingConfirmed`): the landed commit is not the old base sha (a train head equal to base_sha landed nothing: a unit whose squash came out empty) and the base, read AFTER the push, points at or contains it (a later landing moving it further is fine); a refused, failed or unconfirmed push = `train_unlanded`: the PR goes back to queued with attempts + 1 (never closed, no post; the bounce that reaches `limits.bounces` holds it, holdReason bounces, post held). Each landed PR is closed on GitHub with a comment naming the commit (GitHub shows Closed) and is `merged` in Exponential: the worker applies pr_merged itself (issue-lifecycle.json: a landing IS pr_merged). Self-hosted without CI: no checks = lands untested, still serialized and resolved. Merging needs no device; a FIX does: a conflict/failing PR whose opener's device is offline waits, and after `limits.offlineHours` (2) shows in Needs you. UNITS + BATCHES (`batches`, `composeBatch`): a UNIT = a lone PR or a stack (bottom first); #EXP-1711: a stack's eligible part is its READY PREFIX = every ready member whose parent (`parent`, the PR it is based on; none = the member before it) is in the prefix too, so the ready bottom lands as one unit while members above it that still wait (or keep arriving) follow later; no ready bottom = not eligible; readyAt = the prefix's latest member's; queue = Merge now units first, then readyAt, ties by the lowest PR number; a batch = whole units in queue order while ≤ `limits.batchMax` (8) PRs, or a smaller server cap (`batchMax` on a case; the instance's MERGE_TRAIN_BATCH_MAX, 1–8, unset = 8); a unit never splits (an oversized stack rides alone); the first unit that does not fit ends the batch (no skipping ahead); a Merge now unit rides alone. Stacks land bottom first: the ready prefix as one unit, the rest once it is ready. CHILDREN (#EXP-1711): a landing CLOSES the PR on the forge, so the forge never restacks: the worker itself takes a landed PR's open children out of any forge-native stack (unstack, every unmerged member) and retargets them onto the base. A live PR still based on an already-landed PR's branch is repaired the same way on the next pass and rides no batch until then, and the worker re-checks at the fast-forward and before a direct merge (#FEED-207: a run whose base landed meanwhile is cancelled and its units re-queued): nothing ever lands onto a landed branch. `pr open` never joins a forge-native stack (a stack here = `base_pull_request_id`), and `pr retarget` unstacks a member the forge refuses to move. Queue position (the pill's `Queued · 2nd`) = the unit's 1-based place in this queue, every member of a stack sharing it. BISECT (`bisect`, `trainRun` over a red oracle: a run is red when it holds a culprit, or while `flaky` runs remain): a red batch is re-run ONCE (`limits.reruns`); red again = bisect by units (left = the first ceil(n/2) units), each half tested on the base as it is then (a landed left half moved it): a green half lands; a red half of one unit = that unit failing (no re-run); a red half of more units bisects again. A batch of one unit red twice = failing. The innocent units of a red batch stay `testing` through the bisect and land with their half. RESOLVER POLICY (`resolver`, `resolveConflicts`): the engine is GENERIC; the repo declares its generated paths in `.exponential/merge-train.json` {`generated`: [{name, paths (repo globs: ** any segments, * within one), strategy, command?}]}. Strategies: `prepend-union` (both sides' prepended entries, newer unit's first: changelogs), `renumber` (the later unit's migration takes the next number, then `command` regenerates the snapshot), `regenerate` (take the base side, run `command`, never compile: bindings, lockfiles, licence inventories), `json-union` (object/array union, the later unit wins a key), `take-later` (binary: the later unit's file). Every conflicted path matched (first rule wins) = resolved, one step per rule in policy order; ANY unmatched path = `conflict` naming only the unmatched files (the unit bounces); #EXP-1711: a unit that conflicts only BEHIND earlier units of its batch (it composes clean on the bare base) reports `against: batch` and is NO bounce: the worker re-queues it without a post, and it composes again once those land. A conflict in a SOURCE (contract.json, icons.json) is unmatched: only generated outputs resolve. `repoPolicy` = this repo's file (`.exponential/merge-train.json`, test-locked equal). PIPELINE (`pipeline`, #EXP-1708, provider-neutral; its own `$comment` is the spec): the worker dispatches it per batch attempt, it composes `exp-train/<train_id>` and reports ONE `exp-train` result; `trainVerdict` folds that result with the forge's checks at the composed sha and the base branch's required set. pr_merge (`texts`, `routing`): ONE waking message type, kind = merged | conflict | failing | held (session-chat.json copy.events `pr_merge`); the PR's line goes to its OPENER while live, else the chat's ROOT (an ended root keeps it for display only, pre-consumed, never woken). merged and a held by the limits (bounces/timeout; never a person's Hold) ALSO reach the root starter's Assistant conversation (agent-settings.json role assistant: 'the main agent that manages every ... pull request they have'), as ONE line per landed batch per Assistant (`assistantBatch`: `Merged #A, #B into master (issues: EXP-1, …)`, its PRs in landing order, issues deduplicated, five then +N; no Assistant = no line, never created for this), and never twice when that conversation already is the PR's target. Agents never poll: after `pr open` they end their turn. NEEDS YOU (`stuckRow`): a PR held by the limits, or conflict/failing with the opener's device offline 2 h+, is ONE needs-you.json row kind `pr` (opens `results`): title `Auto-merge stuck on #N`, meta = the reason (`3 bounces`, `24 hours`, `Device offline`), its actions as THE Button sm row: Retry (= resume), Merge now (owners: the `mergeNowPrompt` alert card, `titleStack` when the PR sits in an open stack, exactly as the `…` menu asks), Close PR (close-pr.json). A person's Hold is never a row. In `auto` mode the EXP-1699 ready-to-merge PR rows go away (no PR waits for a person); in `approval` mode they stay and their tap is Needs approval (THE pill's confirm: the plain or the stack confirm, Merge queues it; never the chat or Results) (needs-you.json prCases carry `mergeMode`). OFFLINE SINCE (`offlineSince`, the `deviceOfflineSince` every client feeds `stuckRow`; #EXP-1710 Danny 2026-11-06): the opener = the PR's `sessionId` session (else its root); no opener or an opener without a device = null (nothing to wait for); its device online (THE device presence every client already shows) = null; else its device row's `lastSeenAt` when synced, and an UNKNOWN last-seen (no device row synced, or `lastSeenAt` null) = the PR's `updatedAt` (its last write, which the move to conflict/failing is: offline since the PR went conflict/failing), never online. The server computes no stuck row. STATUS PILL (`statusPill`, replaced the old Merge pill): THE header pill (session-chat.json guidePullRequest; phones: the bottom Merge capsule shows the same) = THE Pill md, mode action, NOT primary, a STATUS: its tap opens the existing Checks submenu (pr-checks.json CHECKS LIST; no rows = mode readonly, tap null). Glyph by icons.json concept, `spinner` = THE Spinner, tone red tints the glyph only. draft `Draft` pr-draft; checks `Checks running` spinner (or `Session working` spinner while only the opener's subtree is busy); queued `Queued · 2nd` ci-queued (ordinal: 1st 2nd 3rd 4th 11th 12th 13th 21st); testing `Testing with 3` spinner (3 = the OTHER PRs of its batch; alone = `Testing`); merged `Merged` pr-merged; conflict `Conflict` pr-conflict red; failing `Checks failing` ci-failed red; held `On hold` pr-hold (a person's) | `Auto-merge stuck` pr-hold red (the limits). THE ONLY ACTION: `approval` mode, ready but not approved = `Needs approval`, PRIMARY, pr-merged, tap approve = the plain or stack confirm (prompts.json merge-issue-pr / merge-run-pr / the stack confirm, as the Merge pill asked), and Merge queues it (never merges directly). The person's merge is otherwise gone from the pill. MENU (`menu`, `mergeMenuEntries`, the header `…`): `checks` (any viewer, the PR has rows), `merge-now` (OWNERS; a live PR not draft, merged or conflict; THE shared alert card `mergeNowPrompt`, Merge destructive, Cancel focused; a stack member lands its whole stack), `hold` | `resume` (members; a live PR not draft or merged; `resume` while held: label `Resume auto-merge`, = Retry), `close-pr` (members, live PR); in that order, icons ui-more submenu rows: checks summary glyph, pr-merged, pr-hold | pr-resume, pr-closed. Merged = checks only. `mergeNowPrompt` joins prompts.json as `merge-now-pr` in ONE PR together with the iOS and Android constants (their tests compare the id set). ROLLOUT (#EXP-1711, Danny 2026-11-08, after the 2026-11-06..08 dogfood): the train is the ONLY merge, for every team and every repository, no server switch; one migration set every team, self-hosted included, to `auto`, and a new team defaults to `auto`. An old client's `yoloMode` write maps onto `merge_mode` (true = auto, false = approval); `yolo_mode` stays a synced column nobody reads until every client reads `merge_mode`. A repository without the pipeline lands serialized and untested (`landDirect`).

pipeline.$comment: EXP-1708: THE TRAIN PIPELINE, provider-neutral (GitHub: `.github/workflows/train.yml` via workflow_dispatch; eCode later runs the same contract). The engine is GENERIC (`scripts/merge-train`: compose.ts, the CLI the pipeline runs from the BASE's checkout, never a unit's): nothing here names this repo; the repo speaks only through `.exponential/merge-train.json` (`setup`, `ci.workflows`, `generated`). DISPATCH: the worker starts ONE run per batch attempt (a re-run or a bisect half = a NEW train_id) with the string inputs `inputs`: `train_id` (the merge_trains row id, [A-Za-z0-9._-]), `base` (the base branch name), `base_sha` (the base the batch composes on = the fast-forward's expected old sha), `mode` (`test` | `untested`: Merge now and teams without CI compose without CI), `units` (JSON, the batch in queue order: [{prs: [{number, head_sha, title, author?}] bottom first, tested_sha?}]; `title` = the final squash title, used once as `{title} (#{number})`; `author` = `Name <email>`; `tested_sha` = a commit whose REQUIRED checks the worker saw green, sent for a lone unit only (GitHub: the PR head)). COMPOSE (runner with git; no build): from base_sha, each PR of each unit in order = a squash merge of head_sha onto the train tip, committed with that title and author. Conflicted paths go through `resolveConflicts` with the repo's `generated`, and so do the unit's paths of a regenerate/renumber rule BOTH the train and the unit changed since their merge base even when git merged them cleanly (two units' generated outputs are stale together; two migrations would share a number); resolved = every rule's file picks first (prepend-union, entry-aware: when base→train and base→unit are each ONE pure insertion and both fit one common split point (the earliest), the file = the base's prefix + the unit's inserted block + the train's inserted block + the base's rest, so each block stays whole entries; a `const <NAME>_<N>` the unit's block declares that the train's file already declares is renumbered to the next free N when the block names it only there; anything else (an edit, a deletion, two insertion points, a name left declared twice) = conflict, never a line union (#LOGS-2: a line union fused three entries into one object); renumber: the base side kept, the later unit's added numbered files under the rule dropped; regenerate: the base side; json-union: deep union, the later unit wins a key, arrays union in order; take-later: the later unit's file, its deletion included), then `setup` once, then each step's `command` in policy order; a renumber's regenerated files matching its `verify` globs must equal the dropped ones' contents (only the name may change), else conflict. A regenerate must KEEP the unit's change (#FEED-212: the lockfiles rule claimed `**/Cargo.lock` but regenerated only apps/desktop, so the train kept master's apps/ede/Cargo.lock and silently dropped #2433's lock change: the composed head was master itself): after the commands, a claimed path the unit changed since the merge base whose composed blob equals the train tip's blob (the base's, for the first unit) while the unit's head blob differs from it = that unit is `conflict` with those files, never a silent keep-ours; so a rule claims only the paths its command regenerates (this repo: `bun.lock`, `apps/desktop/Cargo.lock`, `apps/ede/Cargo.lock`, one `cargo update --workspace` per Cargo workspace; any other Cargo.lock conflict is unmatched = conflict). Unmatched paths, a failing command or a failed verify = that WHOLE unit is `conflict` with its files (unmatched ones, else the rule's paths): the tip resets to before the unit and composing goes on with the next unit. REF: `exp-train/<train_id>` is force-pushed: its head = the composed sha; no unit composed = ONE empty marker commit on base_sha (never lands). The batch diff travels as `base_sha`: CI computes `git diff base_sha head` and runs only the jobs its own path filters hit. CI: mode test and ≥ 1 unit composed: `proven` when the batch is ONE unit with tested_sha and the composed tree equals tested_sha's tree (no run); else every `ci.workflows` entry is started on the ref with input `base_sha` = `dispatched` (no workflows = `none`); mode untested = `skipped` only when, for every composed unit, its `resolved` is empty AND its `drifted` is empty: a Merge now whose compose had to rewrite a conflicted file, or whose lockfile drifted, runs as mode test (`proven` / `dispatched` / `none`), so CI runs on the composed ref and the verdict waits for it (`trainChecksMode`, `checksModes`; #LOGS-2). LOCKFILES (the repo's `lockfiles`, NOTHING hard-coded; this repo: `repoPolicy.lockfiles`): a unit's `drifted` = every path it changed since its merge base with the tip that matches `lockfiles.paths` and whose composed blob differs from the blob at that PR's head_sha (#LOGS-2: #2412 moved apps/ede/Cargo.lock on master, #2420's Merge now merged its own Cargo.lock edit CLEANLY onto it, no rule fired, `cargo fetch --locked` failed on master), plus every lock the TRAIN changed since that merge base named `manifests[].lock` and sitting in the dir or an ancestor dir of a manifest (`manifests[].paths`) the unit changed (a manifest edited against a lock that moved under it); omitted on the outcome when empty. KNOWN GAP: the manifest pairing is by file name and ancestry only: a Cargo workspace member outside its lock's tree, a lock under a different name, or a manifest whose lock is never committed is not paired; nothing composed = `none`. The pipeline never waits for CI. REPORT: ONE result named `check` (`exp-train`) on the ref's head (GitHub: a check run, external_id = train_id, its output.text = the `outcome` JSON; conclusion success when ≥ 1 unit composed, else failure; infra trouble = `error` set, `head` null, conclusion failure, posted on the marker commit when it could still push, else the run fails without one: the worker sees the run completed with no result = error). THE VERDICT (`trainVerdict`, `verdicts`): the worker reads the forge's checks at `head` and the base branch's REQUIRED check names from the forge (GitHub: the branch rules' required_status_checks; NOTHING hard-coded), then: no result yet = pending; error = error; nothing composed = conflict; checks proven/skipped/none or no required checks = green; dispatched: any required check completed with a conclusion other than success/neutral/skipped = red (at once, the rest may still run), any missing or unfinished = pending, else green. `composed` = the units that ride (green = land them by fast-forwarding base to head; red = re-run/bisect per `bisect`), `conflicts` = the units that bounce (`train_conflict`) whatever the state.
